recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not reintroduce ResearchStudy.location for FHIR-14117 because that would conflict with the later FHIR-37641 decision; no core follow-up is recommended for this seed.
issue_request: FHIR-14117 was a Published/Persuasive BRR change request for STU3 ResearchStudy. It requested a better name than jurisdiction for the participating-location concept, and the final resolution recorded changing the element to location for the December 2017 ballot.
initial_application: Git history shows the historical ResearchStudy spreadsheet changed from ResearchStudy.jurisdiction to ResearchStudy.participatingLocation in d8f6af6f29 and 09e837eab3, with 09e837eab3 explicitly tagged GF#14117. The December 2017 ResearchStudy batch commit f09300abf4 then changed ResearchStudy.participatingLocation and its search parameter path/name to ResearchStudy.location, matching the Jira resolution.
additional_context: FHIR-37641 was a later Published/Persuasive with Modification BRR issue for R5 that clarified ResearchStudy.location meant a broad geographic area rather than a precise address, renamed the element to ResearchStudy.region, and updated the short definition. Commits a7c2740146 and 136aeb7fbf implemented that rename and corrected the ResearchStudy search parameter metadata. FHIR-31652 was implemented in the same ResearchStudy commit but concerned AssociatedParty.classifier, not the location rename.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current active ResearchStudy source defines ResearchStudy.region and no longer has a ResearchStudy.jurisdiction or ResearchStudy.participatingLocation element; the remaining participatingLocation text is only a BRIDG mapping to StudyProtocolVersion.participatingLocationCode.

related_jiras.note: Later Published BRR decision renamed ResearchStudy.location to ResearchStudy.region and explains why the current element name differs from the STU3 FHIR-14117 resolution.
Implemented in the same ResearchStudy commit as FHIR-37641 but limited to AssociatedParty.classifier, so it was not decided here.
